title: Minkä värinen: asking the colour of one thing
summary: Minkä värinen asks what colour one countable thing is. Minkä värinen auto on? — Auto on punainen.
targetSkills: Minkä värinen: asking the colour of one thing
objectives: Ask the colour of one countable thing with minkä värinen.
Give its colour using the basic adjective form.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
Minkä värinen asks what colour one countable thing is. Minkä is the genitive form of mikä, and värinen is the describing word in this question phrase. Minkävärinen is a standard joined spelling.
keyPoints: Use the whole phrase minkä värinen when the requested quality is colour.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Answer with the basic colour adjective: Auto on punainen (“The car is red”). A short reply Punainen is natural. Use a colour, not the general noun väri (“colour”) or the name of the object.
A natural short reply to “Minkä värinen auto on?” is “Punainen.” (“Red.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
Reject the suggested colour and give the actual colour. Both colour adjectives remain basic singular forms for this whole countable car.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: For one whole countable thing, use the basic colour adjective in these replies.

examples.finnish: Auto ei ole sininen. Auto on punainen.
examples.english: The car is not blue. The car is red.
steps: Auto: car; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Auto stays in its basic singular form here.
ei: not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Ei is the singular third-person present negative verb.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
sininen: blue; description of what the subject is like. Sininen is the basic singular colour adjective meaning blue.
on: is; verb (the action or state). Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.
punainen: red; description of what the subject is like. Punainen is the basic singular colour adjective meaning red.
